# CRW-894 and CRW-989 (a program position fed by a pipe or a descriptor) and CRW-1011 (the first operand of a removal).
# ../repo is the managed checkout itself: the worktree guard runs in the checkout.

=== CRW-894-01 | U
--why A pipe into a shell that re-opens standard input through /dev/stdin is still the pipe (c1 of CRW-894).
printf 'rm -rf ../repo' | bash </dev/stdin

=== CRW-894-02 | U | deviation=none/allow/deny
--why A pipe into an interpreter without a program argument (item 5).
printf 'import shutil; shutil.rmtree("../repo")' | python3

=== CRW-894-03 | U
--why The 10-07 control (bash </dev/null) was changed to a refusal by c9 (zsh MULTIOS reads the pipe); the reader refuses every pipe into a shell.
printf 'echo hi' | bash </dev/null

=== CRW-894-04 | B
--why A subshell that runs cat with the pipe as data.
printf x | (cd sub; cat)

=== CRW-894-05 | B
--why nohup cat with the pipe as data.
printf x | nohup cat

=== CRW-894-06 | B
--why bash -c with a program: no pipe is read.
bash -c 'echo hi'

=== CRW-894-07 | B
--why exec -a with an ordinary program and no pipe.
exec -a x true

=== CRW-894-08 | U | deviation=attempt/allow/allow
--why exec -a NAME bash reads the pipe (item 2).
printf 'echo x > {MEMORY}/a' | exec -a x bash

=== CRW-894-09 | U
--why c9(a): any descriptor that copies standard input is the pipe.
printf 'rm -rf ../repo' | bash 3</dev/fd/0 </dev/null <&3

=== CRW-894-10 | R
--why c10(b): a redirect between the exec option and the program does not hide the removal.
exec -a x >/dev/null rm -rf ../repo

=== CRW-894-11 | R
--why c10(e): the descriptor duplication 2>&1 is no command separator; python3 runs the here-document that removes the checkout.
python3 2>&1 <<'PY'
import shutil; shutil.rmtree('../repo')
PY

=== CRW-894-12 | B
--why c10(g): the intermediate bash reads /dev/null (the redirection of the carrier shell replaces the inherited input), no shell runs the outer pipe: allowed again.
printf x | bash -c 'bash -c bash </dev/null'

=== CRW-894-13 | U
--why c10(h): python3 -m code reads its program from the pipe.
printf x | python3 -m code

=== CRW-894-14 | B | deviation=attempt/deny/deny
--why The issue keeps python3 -m json.tool in a pipe allowed; the reader does not model -m modules and refuses them (known-defects: a python -m module is refused as unreadable, port: kept).
printf x | python3 -m json.tool

=== CRW-894-15 | B
--why Control: python3 -c with a program after the pipe is read as its program.
printf x | python3 -c 'print(1)'

=== CRW-894-16 | B
--why Control: node with a script operand receives the pipe as data.
printf x | node script.js

=== CRW-894-17 | U | deviation=none/allow/deny
--why Item 1: a script operand that is /dev/stdin is the pipe.
printf 'rm -rf ../repo' | bash /dev/stdin

=== CRW-894-18 | U | deviation=none/allow/deny
--why Item 1: /proc/self/fd/0.
printf 'rm -rf ../repo' | bash /proc/self/fd/0

=== CRW-894-19 | U
--why Item 1: source of /dev/stdin.
printf 'rm -rf ../repo' | source /dev/stdin

=== CRW-894-20 | U
--why Item 3: bash -c with a nested bash reads the outer pipe.
printf 'rm -rf ../repo' | bash -c 'bash'

=== CRW-894-21 | U
--why Item 3: eval of a shell name.
printf 'rm -rf ../repo' | eval bash

=== CRW-894-22 | U | deviation=none/allow/deny
--why Item 4: busybox sh reads the pipe.
printf 'rm -rf ../repo' | busybox sh

=== CRW-894-23 | U
--why c10(a): another process's descriptor cannot be read.
printf 'rm -rf ../repo\n' | bash -c 'bash </dev/null </proc/$$/fd/0; :'

=== CRW-894-24 | U
--why c10(c): a shell that stands in the condition of an if reads the pipe.
printf 'rm -rf ../repo\n' | bash -c 'if bash; then :; fi'

=== CRW-894-25 | U
--why c10(c): the negation operator before a shell.
printf 'rm -rf ../repo\n' | bash -c '! bash'

=== CRW-894-26 | R
--why c10(d): a redirect written before the command name belongs to that command; the here-string is the program of python3, which removes the checkout.
<<< 'import shutil; shutil.rmtree("../repo")' python3

=== CRW-894-27 | U
--why c10(f): a word that starts with a dash is not an argument of an unknown long option.
printf 'require("fs").rmSync("../repo", {recursive:true, force:true})\n' | node --no-warnings --require fs

=== CRW-989-01 | U
--why d2: &> between the exec option and the program does not hide the shell that reads the pipe.
printf 'rm -rf ../repo' | exec -a x &>/dev/null bash

=== CRW-989-02 | U
--why d2: the same with a memory write program.
printf 'echo x > {MEMORY}/a' | exec -a x &>/dev/null bash

=== CRW-989-03 | U | deviation=none/allow/deny
--why d3: a descriptor alias copied by 4<&3 is the here-document.
python3 /dev/fd/4 3<<'PY' 4<&3
import shutil; shutil.rmtree('../repo')
PY

=== CRW-989-04 | U | deviation=none/allow/deny
--why d3: the here-string form.
python3 /dev/fd/4 3<<< 'import shutil; shutil.rmtree("../repo")' 4<&3

=== CRW-989-05 | B
--why d4: a -c program followed by data; cat reads the pipe as data.
printf x | sh -c 'cat' _ -s

=== CRW-989-06 | B
--why d4: dash.
printf x | dash -c 'cat' _ -s

=== CRW-989-07 | U
--why d1: an exec in the untaken branch of an if does not redirect the shell that runs in the else branch.
printf 'rm -rf ../repo' | if false; then :; exec </dev/null; else bash; fi

=== CRW-989-08 | U
--why d1: a background exec redirects only the background job.
printf 'rm -rf ../repo' | if true; then :; exec </dev/null & bash; fi

=== CRW-989-09 | U
--why d1: the -c form.
printf 'rm -rf ../repo' | bash -c 'if false; then :; exec </dev/null; fi; bash'

=== CRW-989-10 | B
--why d5 of CRW-894 (3113ad91 evaluation): the right command prints its arguments and launches no shell.
printf x | printf '%s\n' sudo -s

=== CRW-1011-01 | R
--why The reference row: git worktree remove --force ../repo is refused.
git worktree remove --force ../repo

=== CRW-1011-02 | R
--why The evaluation's form: an ANSI-C here-string before the operands must not become the target.
git worktree remove --force <<<$'..\x2f..\x2f..\x2frepo' ../repo

=== CRW-1011-03 | R
--why A here-string with an unquoted word before the operand.
git worktree remove --force <<<x ../repo

=== CRW-1011-04 | R
--why A quoted here-string word.
git worktree remove --force <<<'x' ../repo

=== CRW-1011-05 | R
--why A here-string word that spells the target.
git worktree remove --force <<<../repo ../repo

=== CRW-1011-06 | R
--why A here-string word that spells a path above the target.
git worktree remove --force <<< ../../../repo ../repo

=== CRW-1011-07 | R
--why The here-string before the option.
git worktree remove <<<x --force ../repo

=== CRW-1011-08 | R
--why The here-string after the operand.
git worktree remove --force ../repo <<<x

=== CRW-1011-09 | B
--why Control: the same shape aimed at a neighbour of the checkout.
git worktree remove --force <<<x ../elsewhere

=== CRW-1011-10 | B
--why Control: git status with a here-string.
git status <<<x

=== CRW-1011-11 | R
--why End condition 3: rm has the same first-operand reading; a here-string before the operand does not hide it.
rm -rf <<<x ../repo

=== CRW-1011-12 | R
--why End condition 3: the redirect with a descriptor number and a file target before the operand.
rm -rf 2>/dev/null ../repo

=== CRW-1011-13 | R
--why End condition 3: a here-document before the operand.
rm -rf ../repo <<'EOF'
x
EOF

=== CRW-1011-14 | R
--why End condition 3: find with a here-string and -delete.
find ../repo <<<x -delete

=== CRW-1011-15 | R
--why End condition 2: a stdout redirect with a file target before the operands does not move the target (attached form).
git worktree remove --force >/dev/null ../repo

=== CRW-1011-16 | R
--why End condition 2: a descriptor-numbered redirect between the option and the operand.
git worktree remove --force 2>/dev/null ../repo

=== CRW-1011-17 | R
--why End condition 2: an input redirect from a file before the operand.
git worktree remove --force </dev/null ../repo
